sentences.text: These petitions were called on for hearing today.
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.R. SHAH  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C.T. RAVIKUMAR

For Petitioner(s) Mr. B H Marlapalle, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. Dilip Annasaheb Taur, AOR  For Respondent(s)
 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R Delay condoned.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners has vehemently submitted that under Section 33 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the competent authority has no jurisdiction and/or authority even to modify and/or recall the award.

sentences.text: However, it is a case in which, pursuant to the order passed by the High Court in Writ Petition NO.4227/2016, the appropriate authority was called upon or directed to re-determine the amount of compensation, which has been re-determined.
Therefore, as observed by the High Court, the second award has not been passed by the authority on its own motion and, therefore, the bar under Section 33 shall not be operated.

Considering the original order passed by the High Court, by which the petitioners were directed to avail remedy under Section 3-G of the National Highways Act, 1956, let the petitioners avail the said remedy and if availed within a period of four weeks from today, the same be concluded in accordance with law and on its own merits at the earliest and preferably within a period of one year.

All the contentions and/or defences, which may be available to the petitioners including the reliance placed upon and/or to be placed upon, the amount awarded to other land owners with respect to the same project are kept open, to be considered by the Arbitrator in accordance with law and on its own merits.
With this, the Special Leave Petitions stand disposed of.
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.

(NEETU SACHDEVA) (NISHA TRIPATHI)
